direction: Champion the impedance-ranked packet probe and treat anti-backdrive latch plus token handoff as optional sub-blocks.
rationale: This angle is closest to the frozen H1 thesis and most directly tests whether cheap source awareness improves startup correctness.
first_step: Implement probe, sequenced startup path, and equal-energy baselines in modular ngspice netlists.
expected_signal: Higher startup success under 1:20 impedance asymmetry and mixed ramps without helper rails.

direction: Keep the dual-path helperless startup as the kill-ready fallback within H1.
rationale: If ranking is too costly, startup-mode selection between two helper-free engines may survive with lower sensing cost.
first_step: Implement passive stacker and burst path sharing one reservoir, then compare against the packet-probe champion.
expected_signal: Faster handoff at the lowest voltages, but only if duplicated path parasitics stay tolerable.

direction: Use mixed-polarity scout buckets as the adversarial differentiator branch.
rationale: This branch targets the least-covered stress case and helps define where the headline claim can remain narrow but material.
first_step: Benchmark dual-bucket startup against single-reservoir OR-ing in mixed-polarity cases.
expected_signal: Lower back-drive loss and fewer false starts when polarity mismatch is present.
